FINAL PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS
A. Brain, right parietal tumor, biopsy: High-grade glioma with a differential of gliosarcoma and anaplastic astrocytoma; see comment.

B. Brain, right parietal tumor, resection: High-grade glioma with a differential of gliosarcoma and anaplastic astrocytoma; see comment.

COMMENT:
Sections reveal a densely cellular and infiltrative glial neoplasm composed of spindle-shaped and xanthomatous tumor cells in fascicular patterns. The tumor displays prominent nuclear atypia with bizarre multinucleated forms. Elevated mitotic activity is noted, up to 15 mitoses per ten high-power fields (2 mm2). Areas of necrosis and microvascular proliferation are present. Occasional eosinophilic granular bodies are observed.
Immunohistochemical stains performed at USC Medical Center on block A3 show the following:
- GFAP: Positive in scattered tumor cells.
- OLIG2: Strong positivity.
- IDH1 R132H mutant protein: Negative.
- ATRX: Retained expression.
- p53: Strong nuclear staining in approximately 60% of tumor cells.
- Ki-67: Labeling index estimated at up to 30%.
- CD34: Positive in numerous tumor cells.
- p16: Retained expression.
- BRAF V600E mutant protein: Shows equivocal staining.
- Reticulin: Highlights focal pericellular deposition.
- SMA: Highlights background blood vessels only.
- MLH1: Retained expression.
- PMS2: Retained expression.
- MSH2: Retained expression.
- MSH6: Retained expression.
Immunohistochemical stains performed at USC Medical Center on block C2 show the following:
- PAS: Highlights rare eosinophilic granular bodies.
- Reticulin: Highlights increased pericellular deposition.
- SMA: Highlights background blood vessels only.
- Desmin: Highlights background blood vessels only.
Immunohistochemical stains performed at USC Medical Center on block C3 show the following:
- GFAP: Positive.
- Reticulin: Does not highlight increased pericellular deposition.
- BRAF V600E mutant protein: Shows equivocal staining.
- CyclinD1: Positive.
Overall, the findings are consistent with a high-grade glioma. The increased reticulin deposition suggests the possibility of an anaplastic astrocytoma (CNS WHO grade 3) and a gliosarcoma (CNS WHO grade 4).
For further genetic characterization, this tumor will be evaluated by the USC Comprehensive Genomics Panel at the USC Clinical Cancer Genomics Laboratory and DNA-based methylation at the NIH. These results will be reported separately, as well as in an addendum if clinically indicated.
This case was discussed at the weekly intradepartmental neuropathology consensus conference.
MGMT methylation analysis will be performed at the USC Molecular Diagnostics Laboratory, and a separate report will follow.
The diagnosis was rendered using whole slide digital images of the glass slides on Philips' FDA-approved (21 CFR 864.3700) PIPS-based platform validated at USC.
All controls performed with the immunohistochemical stains reported above reacted appropriately. These immunohistochemical stains were developed and their performance characteristics determined by the USC Medical Center Department of Pathology. They have not been cleared or approved by the U. S.
